entities.summary: The H class was a series of battleship designs for Nazi Germany's Kriegsmarine, which were intended to fulfill the requirements of Plan Z in the late 1930s and early 1940s. The first variation, "H-39", called for six ships to be built, essentially as enlarged Bismarck-class battleships with 40.6 cm (16 in) guns and diesel propulsion. The "H-41" design improved the "H-39" ship with still larger main guns, eight 42 cm (16.5 in) weapons, and reinforced deck armor. The Construction Office of the Oberkommando der Marine (OKM) concluded their work with the "H-41" design, and were not involved in subsequent plans.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The H-class super battleship design influenced Nazi Germany's naval strategy and contributed to the development of their U-boat fleet. Although ultimately not built, these designs reflected the Kriegsmarine's efforts to counter British naval superiority.
